correctness.rationale: An independent construction is to draw n=N−1 independent Uniform(−1,1) labeled coordinates, then condition on the p−1 lower labels preceding all q upper labels and on the p-th order statistic being nonnegative. This is precisely uniform coordinate volume on the given polytope. Ranks are independent of sorted values, so the probability of the label event is (p−1)!q!/n!, and the transformed p-th order statistic has Beta(p,q) law. The conditioning yields the asserted volume and first sampler; conditioning on H negative draws instead gives H∼Bin(n,1/2) conditioned on H≤p−1, with k=p−1−H and the printed weights and label permutations. This includes p=1 or q=1. The chain count follows because fixing the signs and strict total ranking splits the slice into chambers of coordinate volume 1/n!. For the asymptotics the log kernel has derivative [(p−q)−(N−2)t]/(1−t²) and second derivative at most −(q−1). The boundary scaling t=z/N gives the stated exponential kernel by dominated convergence. The critical scaling t=z/√N gives exp(λz−z²/2) with integrable Gaussian domination on z≥0. In the interior, expand at t_N with t=t_N+z/√N; the normalized curvature tends to −1/[4α(1−α)] and the same curvature bound dominates globally. The volume constants follow by integrating the kernels, including the q prefactor and the value of the kernel at its interior mode. RESULT.md §§1–6 and verification.py were inspected, not executed; the numerical sampler and quadrature are not the basis of this decision.

evidence: The DLMF expansion is uniform for x in (0,1) and shapes with both proportions bounded away from zero. Let ρ=q/N, x=(1−t)/2 and J(x)=ρ log(ρ/x)+(1−ρ) log((1−ρ)/(1−x)). The expansion uses η=sgn(x−ρ)√(2J(x)), a leading normal CDF Φ(√N η), and explicit correction terms, with c0 in Eq. 8.18.11.

The tail P(T>t)=I_x(q,p)/I_{1/2}(q,p) and the volume V=q 2^(N−1) B(p,q) I_{1/2}(q,p) apply identically in all three regimes. For x below and bounded away from ρ, the normal-tail leading coefficient (−1/η) combines with c0 to give I_x(q,p)∼exp(−NJ(x))√[ρ(1−ρ)]/[(ρ−x)√(2πN)]. This controls relative error even in the boundary regime, where a normal CLT alone is insufficient.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier uniform incomplete-beta expansion is stronger than these three leading-order conditional limits, and its shape-proportion hypotheses include all three stated regimes. Access to the triangulation article's full proof is not required for this implication.

evidence: Boundary substitution x=(1−z/N)/2 gives N[J(x)−J(1/2)]→(1−2α)z and a prefactor ratio tending to 1, hence the stated conditional exponential survival. Stirling times the left-tail coefficient gives V∼q/[2N(ρ−1/2)].
Critical substitution x=(1−z/√N)/2 gives √Nη→λ−z and I_{1/2}→Φ(λ), hence survival Φ(λ−z)/Φ(λ). Stirling gives q 2^(N−1)B(p,q)/√N→√(π/2)exp(λ²/2).
In the interior I_{1/2}→1, and x=(1−t_N−z/√N)/2 gives √Nη→−z/[2√(α(1−α))]. Stirling supplies the exponential volume rate α log(2α)+(1−α) log(2(1−α)).

evidence: The conditioning events are exactly fixed labeling of the first p−1 ranks and a bound at zero on the p-th rank among n uniform draws. Fixed ranks do not bias sorted values; given the p-th value, the two groups are independent sorted uniforms on the two intervals, with random within-group labels.

The sign-pattern mixture is exactly a truncated binomial on the number H of negative values: w_k=[(p−1)!q!/(N−1)!] binom(N−1,p−1−k). Conditional on H it is ordinary uniform ranking of the positive draws and independent uniform negative draws.
DLMF 8.17.5 gives the integer incomplete-beta binomial tail; beta symmetry converts its tail direction as needed.

The decisive prior implication instead comes from the exact labeled-order-statistic reduction and classical incomplete-beta formulas, including a stronger uniform transition expansion. The rank/positivity conditioning gives both samplers and the volume directly, and taking a ratio of the same prior beta tails produces all three stated limits with their constants. No separate geometric limit theorem survives this reduction. This is a direct-corollary determination, not a claim that the same title or pinned-slice application was published earlier.

value.rationale: The formulas are correct and useful as a worked example of volume sampling. Under the natural rank representation, however, the chain count and samplers are standard ordering and binomial conditioning, and the three limits are evaluations of a stronger uniform beta expansion. The claimed package offers no independent geometric invariant beyond these mechanical consequences. No supported remainder warrants a substantive repair.
